steps.name: dark: Your Rights panel text contrast

measurements.text: Your rights
This is general information about your rights, not legal advice.
The right to clear information about your care and its cost
Relevant here
measurements.className: text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider rounded-full bg-terracotta/10 text-terracotta px-2 py-0.5 shrink-0

measurements.text: You have the right to a statement you can understand, showing what you were charged and why.
→ Ask your provider to explain any charge in plain language. They must respond.
The right to be told about changes to your care and fees
Relevant here
measurements.className: text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider rounded-full bg-terracotta/10 text-terracotta px-2 py-0.5 shrink-0

measurements.text: Your provider should tell you before your fees or services change, not surprise you afterwards.
→ Ask for written notice of any backdated adjustment or fee change and the reason for it.
The right to raise concerns without it affecting your care
You can give feedback or make a complaint, and your provider cannot treat you differently for doing so.
→ Raise it with your provider first. If it is not resolved, the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission can help.
The right to a free independent advocate
You can have someone speak up alongside you, at no cost, through the Older Persons Advocacy Network.
→ Call OPAN on 1800 700 600 for free, confidential advocacy support.
Aged care Statement of Rights (plain-language summary)
